metadata.stage_title: Level 1. Do Eyes Send Out Rays?

chat_history.content: I believe there is fire in the eye reaching outward toward the visible world. If you disagree, show me why vision must travel not from eye to world, but from world to eye.
in complete darkness the eye does not light objects by itself, so vision must depend on light entering the eye from outside.

You are right that darkness hides light, yet the eye’s inner fire still reaches outward and seeks any illumination that arrives. Vision arises when this fire meets external light, not from the eye alone.
very bright light can injure the eye, which shows the causal action travels into the eye rather than out from it.

The eye’s inner fire seeks light, and when bright rays pour in they can overwhelm that fire, causing injury; yet the fire still initiates vision, meeting external light rather than merely receiving it.
a small opening can project an inverted image of a bright scene, which makes sense if light travels from the object toward the observer.

The opening lets the eye’s inner fire touch the light that comes from the scene; the fire then spreads, turning that light into the inverted image. Thus vision still starts with the eye’s fire meeting external light.
